processing: Handled as sheng generally is: withered, pan-fired, rolled and sun-dried, then pressed or sold loose.
harvest_season: Spring is the prized picking, as usual in Yunnan.
appearance_dry: Large dark green leaf, with buds in better grades, typical of Yunnan maocha.
appearance_wet: Thick mid-green leaves that open fully.
taste_profile: One tasting account of Qianjiazhai old-tree tea describes strong aroma and clear bitterness with slight astringency that clears fast into a good sweet aftertaste.

brewing.notes: Start short, since the reported bitterness is real, then lengthen as the tea settles.

vintage_note: Sold like other sheng, by harvest year, under the regional brand Qianjiazhai or a garden name such as Madeng or Jiujia. Check whether a label means cultivated old gardens or the wild population. The local standard is a Zhenyuan association one, not a national guarantee.
description:
Zhenyuan is a county on the Ailao Mountains in Pu'er prefecture, known in tea mainly for Qianjiazhai, a large population of wild old tea trees in the nature reserve around Jiujia. Most tea sold under the county's name comes from cultivated old gardens nearby rather than from those wild trees.

The gardens grouped under the Qianjiazhai brand include Madeng, Jiujia, Dongsa, Xuetang and Zhangpen. Processing is ordinary sheng work, so differences come from the garden and the age of the trees.

The one specific tasting record to hand describes a fragrant tea with obvious bitterness that resolves quickly. That is a single impression, so treat it as a starting point. Short early steeps are the safe approach.

When buying, read the label closely. Wild-tree tea and cultivated-garden tea are different products, and the wild population is a protected botanical site whose fame gets borrowed freely.
history:
A 1996 expert review recorded the Qianjiazhai wild tree community at 2,100 to 2,500 m in moist evergreen broadleaf forest. The best-known tree, Qianjiazhai No. 1, is often given an age of about 2,700 years, but that figure is an estimate with no carbon dating behind it. Researchers also disagree on whether the population is purely wild or may include trees once planted that went feral.

Madeng tea is the county's older named product. More recently Zhenyuan folded Madeng into a single Qianjiazhai brand and commissioned an association standard from the national pu-erh testing centre.
